tools.name: create_absence
tools.description:
Create one or more absence requests. Executes immediately — there is NO preview/confirm step.

Target employee (managers only): to create for another person, pass 'employee_name' (preferred)
or 'employee_id'. Omit both to create for the current user. Never ask the user for an ID —
resolve the name here. If the name is ambiguous the tool returns the options so you can ask which
one and call again with a more specific name.

Category: pass 'absence_category_name' (partial match) — never ask for an ID. Resolve it with
list_absence_categories when unsure.

Dates: for a single day or a contiguous run, pass 'start_on'/'end_on'. For SEVERAL separate days
(e.g. "1 hour on the 13th, 14th, 15th and 16th"), pass 'dates' (a list of YYYY-MM-DD) — one
absence is created per day, which keeps a partial-hour absence counted per day. Do NOT collapse
separate days into a single start_on..end_on range: a range charges the days in between in full.

Hours: for a partial-day absence pass 'start_hour' and 'end_hour' (HH:MM); 'all_day' is then
treated as false automatically. Otherwise the absence is all-day.

Attachments: if the user attached a supporting document in the chat (e.g. a medical note),
pass its ref in 'attachment_refs' to file it with the absence. With several days, the
document is filed with every absence created.

absence_category_id.description: The ID of the leave category. Use absence_category_name instead when possible.

absence_category_name.description: Category name (partial match). Alternative to absence_category_id. Use this when the user mentions a category by name.

start_on.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Use with end_on for a single day or a contiguous range. Ignored when 'dates' is given.

end_on.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional — defaults to start_on for a single-day absence. Ignored when 'dates' is given.

dates.description: List of individual days (YYYY-MM-DD). Creates one absence per day. Use for non-contiguous days or a per-day time window; do NOT turn separate days into a start_on..end_on range.

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day absence. Defaults to true. Automatically treated as false when start_hour/end_hour are given.

start_hour.description: Start time in HH:MM format (for a partial-day absence)

end_hour.description: End time in HH:MM format (for a partial-day absence)

description.description: Optional description or reason for the absence

employee_name.description: Name of the employee to create the absence for (managers only). Preferred over employee_id. Omit to create for yourself.

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Optional — prefer employee_name. Omit to create for yourself.

approved.description: Whether to automatically approve the absence. Defaults to false. Only available for managers and admins.

attachment_refs.description: Refs of documents the user attached in the chat (the ref="att_N" attribute of a <document>). Pass them to file those documents with the absence (e.g. a medical note). Copy each ref exactly as it appears.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description:
File one or more documents the user attached in the chat (PDF or image) into the employee
document archive (contracts, payslips, certificates…). Executes immediately — there is NO
preview/confirm step.

Requires at least one ref in 'attachment_refs' — the file IS the document. One document is
created per file. Without 'name', each document takes its file's filename.

Category: optional. Pass 'document_category_name' (partial match) — never ask for an ID.
Resolve it with list_document_categories when unsure. Omit it to file without category.

Target employee (managers only): to file in another person's archive, pass 'employee_name'
(preferred) or 'employee_id'. Omit both to file in your own. Never ask the user for an ID —
resolve the name here. If the name is ambiguous the tool returns the options so you can ask
which one and call again with a more specific name.

attachment_refs.description: Refs of the documents the user attached in the chat (the ref="att_N" attribute of a <document>). Required — one document is filed per ref. Copy each ref exactly as it appears.

name.description: Optional name for the document(s). Defaults to each file's filename.

document_category_id.description: The ID of the document category. Use document_category_name instead when possible.

document_category_name.description: Category name (partial match). Alternative to document_category_id. Use this when the user mentions a category by name.

employee_name.description: Name of the employee whose archive to file into (managers only). Preferred over employee_id. Omit to file into your own.

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Optional — prefer employee_name. Omit to file into your own archive.

- TEMPORARY override: pass start_on AND end_on (e.g. "next week") — applies only for that range,

- PERMANENT change: pass start_on with NO end_on (e.g. "from Monday on") — this REPLACES the

tools.name: list_appointments
tools.description:
List appointments booked through the company's booking calendars (the public
scheduling pages where clients, candidates or other guests pick a slot to meet
an employee). An appointment is a scheduled meeting with a named guest. Use
this tool for any question about these scheduled meetings, however the user
happens to phrase it.

Results span every calendar the user can access; you never need to name a
calendar first. Use calendar_name only to narrow to one specific calendar.

Scope of what to return:
- kind selects which calendars count: general (normal booking calendars),
  interviews (recruiting/selection calendars), or all. Choose it from what the
  user is asking about, not from a fixed rule.
- status filters by lifecycle state. With no status you get the actionable
  agenda: confirmed appointments inside the date window, plus every pending one
  (the approval queue) whatever its date, so nothing awaiting the user is missed.
- The date window defaults to from today for ~30 days and bounds the confirmed
  results. To look further back or ahead (e.g. past cancellations), set
  start_date/end_date explicitly.

Times are shown in each calendar's own timezone and always labelled; report
them to the user as given. Use response_format detailed when the user wants
specifics or you may need to act on a specific appointment next.

kind.description: Which calendars to include. 'general' = normal booking calendars (default). 'interviews' = recruiting/selection calendars (choose when the subject is hiring/candidates). 'all' = both (choose when the request isn't limited to one kind).

status.description: Filter by lifecycle state. Omit to get the actionable agenda (confirmed + pending). Use 'pending' for what awaits approval, 'cancelled'/'declined' for the corresponding history.

calendar_name.description: Restrict to a single calendar by name (partial match). Omit to span all accessible calendars.

end_date.description: End of the date window (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to ~30 days after the start.

response_format.description: Response format. 'concise' (default) for summaries; 'detailed' for full data and when you might act on a specific appointment next.

booking calendar): guest, contact, hosts, timing, status, source and any note
attached to it (for example a message left when it was created, approved,
declined or cancelled).

Identify the appointment the way a person would: by the calendar it belongs to
plus the guest's name, optionally narrowed by date. If a previous listing
already surfaced an internal appointment id, you may pass it directly instead —
prefer the human identifiers, fall back to the id only when name+date is
ambiguous or awkward. If more than one appointment matches, the tool asks you
to narrow it down.

Times are shown in the calendar's timezone and always labelled.

tools.name: manage_appointment
tools.description:
Decide on an existing appointment: approve, decline or cancel it. Every decision
emails the guest, so this returns a preview first and applies nothing until you
confirm it. Only call it once the user has clearly asked to act on a specific
appointment. If they are still choosing which one, or only asking about it,
don't act yet: identify the appointment and the intended action first.

Which actions are possible depends on the appointment's current state, so read
it (or list appointments) when unsure:
- approve turns a pending (or previously cancelled) appointment into confirmed.
- decline rejects an appointment that is still pending.
- cancel calls off a confirmed or pending appointment, freeing the slot.
If the requested action doesn't fit the current state, the tool explains why
instead of acting.

Identify the appointment by calendar name + guest name (optionally a date), or
by an internal id from a previous detailed listing. When approving or declining,
an optional message can be sent to the guest along with the decision;
cancellations send a standard notice and cannot carry a message.

calendar_name.description: Name of the calendar the appointment belongs to (partial match). Use with invitee_name.

invitee_name.description: Name of the guest who booked (partial match). Use with calendar_name.

appointment_id.description: Internal appointment id from a previous detailed listing. Optional shortcut; human identifiers preferred.

client_message.description: Optional message shared with the guest when approving or declining. Ignored on cancel — the guest receives a standard cancellation notice.

tools.name: create_appointment
tools.description:
Book an appointment manually on one of the company's general booking calendars —
for example when arranging a meeting on someone's behalf. It creates a confirmed
appointment straight away and (optionally) emails the guest; there is no separate
confirmation step, so only call it once the user has clearly asked to book, with
the guest, date and time settled. While details are still being discussed, hold
off and gather them first.

This is for general calendars only. Interview/recruiting calendars are booked by
the candidate through their invitation, not created here.

Times are interpreted in the calendar's own timezone. Hosts default to how the
calendar is configured (its single host, or all required hosts) — only pass
host names to override that. If the requested slot clashes with a host's
existing booking, the tool reports it instead of double-booking. If you are not
sure a time is actually free, check the calendar's open times first
(list_appointment_slots) rather than guessing one.

tools.name: list_appointment_slots

Show the free time slots a booking calendar currently offers, so you can propose
real, bookable times before creating an appointment. Availability is derived from

calendar's rules (duration, notice, buffers, horizon) — so only genuinely
open slots are returned.

tools.name: create_survey
tools.description:
Create a survey (poll, feedback, climate or NPS) with its sections and questions in one step. It is
created right away as a DRAFT — inert (not active, not visible to anyone) and fully editable until
someone activates it from the admin panel.

If the user is still designing it with you — helping write questions, weighing sections, undecided on
the structure — shape it together first. Otherwise, when the structure is sound (which a clear request
often gives you outright), create the draft and present the result. Read the conversation, not just the
wording.

For NPS surveys: only pass name and nps_question — the standard 0-10 scale is created automatically.
For poll/feedback/climate: pass sections with questions. Each question needs a text and type.

Question types:
- 'rating': a numeric scale (e.g., 1-5 stars). Set 'scale' (3-10, default 5). Options are created automatically.
- 'selection': multiple choice. Pass 'options' as an array of strings.
- 'yes_no': binary choice. Automatically creates Yes/No options.
- 'text': open text response. No options needed.
- 'date_time': date and/or time response. Set 'datetime_response_type' to only_date, only_time, or date_and_time.

Examples:
- "create a survey about workplace safety" → type=feedback, suggest 5-8 questions mixing rating and text
- "create an NPS survey for the onboarding program" → type=nps, nps_question="How likely are you to recommend our onboarding program to a new colleague?"
- "make a poll about the office party" → type=poll, short with 2-3 selection questions

This tool does NOT activate the survey or configure visibilities.
After creation, tell the user: the survey is now a draft, they can review/edit it, and they need to
configure visibility (who receives it) and activate it from the admin panel when ready.

name.description: Survey name. Choose something clear and descriptive. Example: 'Workplace Safety Assessment Q1 2026'

type.description: Survey type. 'poll' = quick vote on a topic (1-3 questions). 'feedback' = structured feedback collection (5-10 questions). 'climate' = workplace climate assessment (typically 10-20 questions across multiple sections). 'nps' = Net Promoter Score (automatic 0-10 scale, just provide the question text). When the user says 'survey' without specifying, use 'feedback'.

anonymous.description: Anonymous survey — responses cannot be attributed to individuals. Default: false. Use true when asking about sensitive topics (climate, complaints, honest feedback about management).

employees_view_answers.description: Whether employees can see aggregated results after the survey closes. Default: false. Recommend true for transparency on climate/NPS surveys.

managers_view_answers.description: Whether managers can see results. Default: false. Almost always should be true.

nps_question.description: ONLY for NPS surveys. The main question text shown with the 0-10 scale. Example: 'How likely are you to recommend working at [Company] to a friend or colleague?' Ignored for non-NPS types.

nps_comments.description: ONLY for NPS surveys. Whether to add an optional comment field after the rating. Default: true. Recommended — comments explain the score.

sections.description: ONLY for poll/feedback/climate surveys. Array of sections, each containing questions. NPS surveys ignore this — they have automatic questions. If you have only one section, still wrap it in an array.

name.description: Section name shown as a heading. Example: 'Work Environment', 'Management', 'Growth Opportunities'. For single-section surveys, use the survey topic as the section name.

text.description: The question text. Write clear, neutral questions. Avoid leading questions. Example: 'How satisfied are you with the communication from your direct manager?' NOT 'Don't you think communication is bad?'

type.description: Question type. 'rating' = numeric scale (use for satisfaction, agreement, frequency). 'selection' = multiple choice (use for categorical choices). 'yes_no' = binary yes/no (use for factual questions). 'text' = open text (use for opinions, suggestions — limit to 1-2 per section to avoid survey fatigue). 'date_time' = date/time answer.

scale.description: ONLY for 'rating' type. Number of points in the scale: 5 = '1 to 5' (default, good for most cases), 10 = '0 to 10' (use for NPS-style detail). Range: 3-10.

options.description: ONLY for 'selection' type. The choices available. Example: ['Very satisfied', 'Satisfied', 'Neutral', 'Dissatisfied', 'Very dissatisfied']. Order matters — first option gets value 0, second gets value 1, etc.

multiple_choice.description: ONLY for 'selection' type. Whether the user can select multiple options. Default: false.

datetime_response_type.description: ONLY for 'date_time' type. 'only_date' shows a date field, 'only_time' shows a time field, and 'date_and_time' shows a combined date/time field. Default: only_date.

mandatory.description: Whether this question requires an answer. Default: true. Set to false for optional text questions like 'Any additional comments?'

tools.name: create_evaluation
tools.description:
Create a performance evaluation process. The evaluation is created in DRAFT status.
Use this when the user wants to set up a 360° review, performance evaluation, or competency assessment.

You configure WHO evaluates (self, direct manager, team manager, office manager) — not the questions.
Question are generated automatically from the company's competencies when the evaluation is activated.

Examples:
- "create a performance evaluation" → name="Performance Evaluation Q1 2026", self_evaluation=true, direct_manager=true
- "set up 360 reviews" → enable all evaluator types (self + direct_manager + team_manager + office_manager)
- "create a self-assessment" → self_evaluation=true, all others false

This tool does NOT activate the evaluation, configure visibilities, or generate questions.
After creation, tell the user: the evaluation is in draft. They need to configure visibilities
(who gets evaluated) and activate it. Question will be generated from the company's competencies.
If no competencies are configured, suggest they set those up first.

name.description: Evaluation name. Example: 'Performance Evaluation H1 2026', '360° Review Q2'

self_evaluation.description: Employees evaluate themselves. Default: false. Recommended for 360° reviews.

direct_manager.description: Direct manager evaluates. Default: false. Most common evaluator type.

team_manager.description: Team manager evaluates. Default: false. Use when team structure is important.

office_manager.description: Office manager evaluates. Default: false. Use for multi-office companies.

anonymous.description: Anonymous evaluation. Default: false. When true, evaluated employees can't see who gave which scores.

employees_view_answers.description: Employees can see their own evaluation results. Default: false. Recommended true for development-focused evaluations.

managers_view_answers.description: Managers can see results. Default: false. Almost always should be true.

tools.name: list_surveys
tools.description:
List surveys. Default scope is 'mine' (surveys the user needs to answer).
Use scope='managed' to see surveys the user manages or created (managers only).
Filter by type: poll, feedback, nps, climate.
Filter by status: active, closed, all (default).
For scope=mine, shows your answering progress (not started, in progress, completed).
For scope=managed, shows participation rates (X of Y responded).
Examples: 'what surveys do I have pending' -> scope=mine, status=active.
'how is the NPS going' -> scope=managed, type=nps. 'climate survey' -> type=climate.
Note: performance evaluations are NOT listed here — use list_evaluations instead.

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = surveys the user needs to answer (default). Shows personal answering progress. 'managed' = surveys the user manages or created. Shows participation rates. When the user says 'my surveys' or 'what do I need to answer' use 'mine'. When they ask 'how is the survey going' or about participation, use 'managed'.

status.description: Filter by survey status. 'active' = currently collecting responses. 'closed' = finished. 'all' = both (default).

type.description: Filter by survey type. 'poll' = quick polls. 'feedback' = feedback surveys. 'nps' = Net Promoter Score. 'climate' = company climate survey. Leave empty for all types.

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for summaries with participation. Use 'detailed' for full survey info including sections and question count.

tools.name: get_survey_results
tools.description:
Get aggregated results for a specific survey. Resolve survey by name — never ask for an ID.
For NPS surveys: calculates NPS score, promoters/passives/detractors breakdown.
For other surveys: shows per-question averages and response distributions.
Respects anonymous surveys — never attributes answers to individuals.
Shows participation rate (responded vs total).
If the survey is still active, shows partial results with a warning.
Examples: 'NPS results' -> type=nps. 'satisfaction survey results' -> survey_name=satisfaction.
'climate survey results' -> type=climate. 'feedback results' -> type=feedback.
When the user mentions a survey type (NPS, climate, feedback, poll), always pass the type parameter.

survey_name.description: Survey name (partial match). Use when the user asks about results for a specific survey. Resolve ambiguity by asking the user.

survey_id.description: Direct survey ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous list_surveys call.

type.description: Filter by survey type. Use when the user asks about a specific type like 'NPS results' -> type=nps. Helps disambiguate when multiple surveys exist.

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for score summaries. Use 'detailed' to include text responses (first 10, truncated) and per-option breakdowns.

tools.name: list_evaluations
tools.description:
List performance evaluations. Default scope is 'mine' (evaluations the user needs to complete as evaluator).
Use scope='managed' to see evaluations the user manages (managers only).
For scope=mine: shows which employees you need to evaluate and your completion status.
For scope=managed: shows overall participation (X of Y evaluators completed).
Filter by status: active (in progress), closed (finished), all (default).
Examples: 'what do I need to evaluate' -> scope=mine, status=active.
'how are evaluations going' -> scope=managed. 'past evaluations' -> status=closed.
Note: this only shows performance evaluations, not regular surveys.

scope.description: Data scope. 'mine' = evaluations where the user is an evaluator (default). Shows which employees to evaluate and completion status. 'managed' = evaluations the user manages. Shows overall participation. When the user asks 'what do I need to evaluate' use 'mine'. When they ask 'how are evaluations going' use 'managed'.

status.description: Filter by evaluation status. 'active' = currently in progress. 'closed' = finished with results available. 'all' = both (default).

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for summary with participation. Use 'detailed' to see evaluated employees, competencies assessed, and evaluator breakdown.

tools.name: get_evaluation_results
tools.description:
Get performance evaluation results by competency for an employee.
Resolve evaluation by name — never ask for an ID.
Default is viewing your own results. Use employee_name to see a reportee's results (managers only).
Shows competency scores with targets and evaluator completion status.
Access is strictly controlled. Managers and evaluation owners can see partial results while active.
Regular employees see results only after the evaluation closes (if sharing is enabled).
Respects anonymous evaluations — never reveals individual evaluator scores.
Examples: 'my evaluation results' -> no employee_name. 'Emma results in Q4 review' -> employee_name=Emma, survey_name=Q4.

survey_name.description: Evaluation name (partial match). Use when the user asks about results for a specific evaluation.

survey_id.description: Direct survey ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous list_evaluations call.

employee_name.description: Employee to view results for (partial match). Leave empty to see own results. Use when asking about a specific person's evaluation.

employee_id.description: Direct employee ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for competency score summary. Use 'detailed' for per-evaluator-type breakdown.

tools.name: list_job_offers
tools.description:
List job offers. Default shows active offers. Use status='archived' for past offers.
In concise format: shows offer title, status, candidate count, and time remaining.
In detailed format: shows full pipeline with candidates per step, ordered by affinity.
Examples: 'open positions' -> status=active. 'Senior Developer offer' -> name=Senior Developer.
'archived offers' -> status=archived. 'how is recruitment going' -> status=active.
Use this to get an overview before drilling into specific candidates.

status.description: Filter by offer status. 'active' = currently accepting applications (default). 'archived' = past offers. 'all' = both.

name.description: Search by job offer title (partial match). Examples: 'backend', 'senior', 'marketing'.

job_offer_id.description: Direct job offer ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for offer list with candidate counts. Use 'detailed' to see the full recruitment pipeline with candidates per step.

tools.name: create_job_offer
tools.description:
Create a new job offer / job posting.
Use when the user wants to publish a position, create a job listing, or start recruiting.

Resolve all references by name — office, categories, skills, job template.
If a job template is provided, pipeline steps (interview stages) are created automatically from it.

Salary is in the company's currency. Dates default to next Monday (start) and +1 month (end).
All category fields default to the first option in the company if not specified.

Examples:
- "create a job offer for a senior developer" → title="Senior Developer", suggest description, skills
- "post a marketing position in the Barcelona office" → title="Marketing Specialist", office_name="Barcelona"
- "create a job offer for an intern, no salary" → title="Intern", salary_min=0, salary_max=0

This tool does NOT publish the offer publicly — it creates it in the admin panel.
The user needs to configure visibility and ensure dates are correct for public display.

title.description: Job title. Clear and professional. Example: 'Senior Backend Developer', 'Marketing Manager'

description.description: Job description in plain text or markdown. Include responsibilities, requirements, and benefits. If the user doesn't provide one, suggest writing one — it's important for attracting candidates.

office_name.description: Office name (partial match). Default: current user's office. Use when the position is in a different office.

office_id.description: Office ID. Use office_name instead when possible.

job_template_name.description: Job template name (defines the recruitment pipeline steps). If not provided, the offer is created without pipeline steps — the user can add them manually later.

job_category_name.description: Job category (partial match). Example: 'Engineering', 'Marketing'. Default: first category in the company.

contract_category_name.description: Contract type (partial match). Example: 'Jornada completa', 'Temporal', 'Prácticas'. When the user says 'becario' or 'prácticas', use this. Default: first contract type.

working_category_name.description: Working arrangement (partial match). Example: 'On-site', 'Remote', 'Hybrid'. Default: first option in the company.

salary_min.description: Minimum salary (annual, company currency). If not mentioned by user, use 0 or ask. Do not invent values. Default: 0.

salary_max.description: Maximum salary (annual, company currency). If not mentioned by user, use 0 or ask. Do not invent values. Default: 0.

start_on.description: Start date for accepting applications (YYYY-MM-DD). Default: next Monday.

end_on.description: End date for applications (YYYY-MM-DD). Default: 1 month from start.

skill_name.description: Skill name (partial match against company's skill catalog).

skills.description: Required skills for the position. Resolved by name against the company's skill catalog. Skill not found are silently skipped with a note in the response.

tools.name: update_job_offer
tools.description:
Update an existing job offer.
Use when the user wants to modify a job posting — title, salary, dates, description, skills.

Resolve the job offer by name or ID. Resolve categories and skills by name.
Only pass the fields you want to change — unchanged fields are kept as-is.

For skills: pass the COMPLETE desired skills list. Existing skills not in the list are removed,
new ones are added. This replaces the current skills, it does not append.

Examples:
- "update the senior developer offer salary to 50-60k" → job_offer_name="Senior Developer", salary_min=50000, salary_max=60000
- "extend the marketing position deadline" → job_offer_name="Marketing", end_on="2026-06-30"
- "archive the old intern position" → job_offer_name="Intern", archived=true

job_offer_id.description: Job offer ID from a previous list_job_offers call.

job_offer_name.description: Job offer title (partial match). Use this when the user refers to the offer by name.

description.description: New job description in plain text or markdown.

office_id.description: Office ID. Use office_name instead when possible.

salary_min.description: Minimum salary (in company's currency, annual). Example: 35000

salary_max.description: Maximum salary (in company's currency, annual). Example: 50000

tags.description: Tags for categorization. Replaces existing tags.

archived.description: Set to true to archive the offer (stops accepting applications). Set to false to reactivate.

skill_name.description: Skill name (partial match against company's skill catalog).

skills.description: Required skills. REPLACES all current skills — pass the complete desired list.

tools.name: create_onboarding_template
tools.description:
Create an onboarding process template with actions/tasks.
Use when the user wants to design an onboarding plan, create onboarding steps, or set up a new hire checklist.

IMPORTANT: This creates a TEMPLATE, not an onboarding for a specific employee.
Template are automatically assigned to new employees based on visibility rules.
The user cannot start an onboarding for a specific employee through this tool.

Actions define what needs to happen and when, relative to the employee's start date:
- phase 'before_start': action happens X days/weeks/months BEFORE the employee starts
- phase 'after_start': action happens X days/weeks/months AFTER the employee starts
- days=0 with after_start: action happens on the start date itself

Examples:
- "create an onboarding for developers" → name="Developer Onboarding", actions with setup laptop, IDE, repo access, etc.
- "create a simple onboarding checklist" → name="General Onboarding", 5-7 common actions
- "make an onboarding with tasks before and after start" → mix of before_start and after_start phases

Suggest a good set of actions when the user gives a vague request. Think about:
- Before start: equipment setup, accounts creation, workspace preparation
- First day: welcome, tour, team introduction, paperwork
- First week: training, tools setup, buddy introduction
- First month: 30-day check-in, goal setting, feedback session

name.description: Template name. Descriptive and specific. Example: 'Engineering Team Onboarding', 'Sales New Hire Checklist'

actions.description: List of onboarding actions/tasks. Each action defines WHAT needs to happen, WHEN (relative to start date), and WHO is responsible.

name.description: Action name. Short and clear. Must be unique within the template.

description.description: Detailed description of what needs to be done.

responsible.description: Who performs this action. 'direct' = the new employee themselves (default). 'team_manager' = their team manager. 'office_manager' = the office manager. 'specific' = a named employee (requires responsible_employee_name with a real person's name, NOT a department like 'HR').

responsible_employee_name.description: ONLY when responsible='specific'. Name of the person responsible (partial match).

days.description: Number of days/weeks/months before or after start date. Default: 0.

phase.description: When relative to start date. 'before_start' = before arrival. 'after_start' = after start (default).

send_notification.description: Send email notification when action is due. Default: false.

needs_approval.description: Whether action needs manager approval. Default: false.

tools.name: update_onboarding_template
tools.description:
Update an existing onboarding template — rename it, add new actions, or remove existing actions.

Resolve the template by name or ID.
To add actions: pass them in 'add_actions' (same format as create).
To remove actions: pass action names in 'remove_actions'.
To rename: pass new 'name'.

You can add and remove actions in the same call.
Action names must be unique within the template — adding a duplicate name will fail.

Examples:
- "add a 90-day review to the engineering onboarding" → template_name="Engineering", add_actions=[{name: "90-day review", days: 90, phase: "after_start"}]
- "remove the laptop setup from the sales onboarding" → template_name="Sales", remove_actions=["Set up laptop"]
- "rename the general onboarding to 'Standard Onboarding'" → template_name="General", name="Standard Onboarding"

add_actions.description: Actions to add (same format as create_onboarding_template actions).

remove_actions.description: Names of actions to remove from the template.

tools.name: list_meeting_templates
tools.description:
List meeting question templates for 1:1s and hiring interviews.
A template is a reusable set of questions. show_in_meeting makes it available in 1:1s.
show_in_job_step plus assigned hiring steps makes it available in candidate interviews.
Use this before creating a new set, and to get IDs for update_meeting_template.
These are NOT survey questions — use list_surveys / create_survey for those.

for.description: Limit to templates used in 1:1 meetings, or templates used in hiring steps. Omit to list all.

response_format.description: Use 'concise' (default) for a one-line summary per template. Use 'detailed' for questions, assignment, and IDs.

tools.name: create_meeting_template
tools.description:
Create a meeting question template with optional questions and assignment.
Use when the user wants interview questions, 1:1 questions, or a reusable question set
for meetings or hiring steps.

This creates a TEMPLATE, not a question asked in a specific meeting today.
Questions are free-text prompts (name + optional tags). They are not survey rating questions.

show_in_meeting=true makes the set available in 1:1s.
show_in_job_step=true plus job_step_template_names assigns it to hiring pipeline steps.
Resolve step names from list_meeting_templates (detailed) or the names the user gives.
If a name is ambiguous, ask the user to be more specific — do not guess.

Examples:
- "create first-interview questions about the company" → show_in_job_step=true, job_step_template_names=["First interview"]
- "make a 1:1 feedback question set" → show_in_meeting=true, show_in_job_step=false

name.description: Template name. Specific, e.g. 'First interview — company'.

description.description: What this set is for.

show_in_job_step.description: Available in hiring interviews. Default: true.

job_step_template_names.description: Hiring pipeline step names to assign (partial match). Required in practice when show_in_job_step is true.

questions.description: Questions to add. Each needs text. Tags are optional.

tools.name: update_meeting_template
tools.description:
Update a meeting question template: rename it, change 1:1 / hiring-step flags,
replace hiring-step assignment, and add, edit, or remove questions.

Resolve the template with template_id or template_name (partial match).
Question names are matched inside that template. If several questions share a name,
use question_id from list_meeting_templates detailed output.

Removing a question that has already been asked in a meeting or interview will fail.
Replacing job_step_template_names replaces the whole assignment set.

template_id.description: Meeting template ID from a previous tool call.

description.description: New description.

show_in_meeting.description: Whether this set is available in 1:1s.

show_in_job_step.description: Whether this set is available in hiring interviews.

job_step_template_names.description: Replace assigned hiring steps with these names. Pass [] to clear.

remove_questions.description: Question names or IDs to remove.

tools.name: delete_meeting_template
tools.description:
Delete a meeting question template. It must have no questions left — remove questions
with update_meeting_template first. Resolve with template_id or template_name.

template_id.description: Meeting template ID from a previous tool call.

tools.name: list_candidates
tools.description:
List candidates. Search by name or filter by job offer.
In concise format: shows name, current step, and affinity score.
In detailed format: shows skills (with job requirement match), ratings, and activity timeline.
Examples: 'candidates for Senior Developer' -> job_offer_name=Senior Developer.
'tell me about Carlos' -> name=Carlos, response_format=detailed.
'all candidates' -> no filters.
When the user asks about a specific candidate, use name with detailed format.

name.description: Search by candidate name (partial match). Use when the user asks about a specific candidate.

job_offer_name.description: Filter candidates from a specific job offer (partial match). Use when the user says 'candidates for [offer]'.

job_offer_id.description: Direct job offer ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

candidate_id.description: Direct candidate ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

response_format.description: Response format. Use 'concise' (default) for candidate list with step and affinity. Use 'detailed' for full profile: skills, ratings, and timeline.

tools.name: move_candidate
tools.description:
Move a candidate to a different step in the recruitment pipeline.
Resolve candidate and step by name — never ask for IDs.
If the candidate has applications in multiple job offers and no offer is specified, asks for clarification.
Steps that email the candidate return a preview to confirm first; the rest move them right away.
Read the result to know which happened: a preview means nothing has changed yet.
If unsure about the step name, call list_job_offers with detailed format first to see available pipeline steps.
Examples: 'move Carlos to Second Interview' -> candidate_name=Carlos, step_name=Second Interview.
'advance Ana to Offer for the backend position' -> candidate_name=Ana, step_name=Offer, job_offer_name=backend.

candidate_name.description: Candidate name (partial match). Use when the user mentions a candidate by name.

candidate_id.description: Direct candidate ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

step_name.description: Target pipeline step name (partial match). Examples: 'Second Interview', 'Offer', 'Discarded'.

step_id.description: Direct step ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

job_offer_name.description: Job offer name for disambiguation. Use when the candidate is in multiple offers and the user specifies which one.

job_offer_id.description: Direct job offer ID for disambiguation.

tools.name: rate_candidate
tools.description:
Rate a candidate on a scale of 1 to 5. Resolve candidate by name — never ask for an ID.
Reports the new average rating after applying it.
Automatically recalculates the candidate's affinity score after rating.
If the candidate is in multiple job offers, use job_offer_name to disambiguate.
If you can't resolve the candidate by name, call list_candidates first to find the correct candidate.
Examples: 'rate Carlos with a 4' -> candidate_name=Carlos, rating=4.
'give Ana a 5 for the backend position' -> candidate_name=Ana, rating=5, job_offer_name=backend.

candidate_name.description: Candidate name (partial match). Use when the user mentions a candidate by name.

candidate_id.description: Direct candidate ID. Use this when you have the ID from a previous tool call.

rating.description: Rating value from 1 to 5. Required. 1 = poor, 5 = excellent.

job_offer_name.description: Job offer name for disambiguation. Use when the candidate is in multiple offers.

job_offer_id.description: Direct job offer ID for disambiguation.

tools.name: get_employee
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific employee. Use when the user asks about
a person's details, role, team, contract, or organizational position.

Resolve employee by name (partial match). If multiple matches, asks user to clarify.

Returns different levels of detail based on permissions:
- Everyone can see: name, email, team, office, manager, role, start date
- Managers and self can see: contract details, leave days, skills
- Sensitive data (salary) follows the same permission rules as the admin panel

If no name or ID is provided, returns the current user's own information.

Examples:
- "show me my info" → no params needed (returns current user)
- "who is Maria's manager?" → employee_name="Maria" (concise format is enough)
- "tell me about the new developer Juan" → employee_name="Juan", response_format="detailed"
- "what team is Sarah on?" → employee_name="Sarah"
- "show me Pedro's contract details" → employee_name="Pedro", response_format="detailed"

For listing multiple employees, use list_employees instead.
This tool is for getting in-depth info about ONE specific person.

employee_name.description: Employee name (partial match). Example: 'María', 'García', 'María García'.

employee_id.description: Employee ID. Use employee_name instead when possible.

response_format.description: Response detail level. 'concise' (default) = name, email, team, office, manager, role, start date. 'detailed' = adds contract info, leave days, skills, direct reports count. Use 'detailed' when you need the employee_id for follow-up tool calls.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description:
Create a task within a project or goal.
Use when the user wants to add a task, todo, or work item to a project.

Task always belong to a project or goal — resolve it by name.
Task are placed in a task list (like a column in a kanban board). Default: first list in the project.
The current user is set as the task creator. Additional employees can be assigned.

Task dates must fall within the project's date range.
If the project has lists like 'Pending', 'In Progress', 'Done', use task_list_name to place the task.

Examples:
- "add a task to the Marketing project" → project_name="Marketing", name="[from user context]"
- "create a task for Maria in Project X" → project_name="Project X", assigned_employees=["Maria"]
- "add a task to the Done list" → task_list_name="Done" (if list has mark_as_completed, progress auto-sets to 100)

This tool creates the task and optionally assigns employees (who receive a notification).
The task starts with progress 0 unless placed in a list that auto-completes.

name.description: Task name. Clear and actionable. Example: 'Design landing page mockup', 'Review Q1 budget report'

project_name.description: Name of the project or goal (partial match, resolved internally). Just pass the name — do NOT search for projects first. Task MUST belong to a project or goal.

project_id.description: Project/goal ID. Use project_name instead when possible.

task_list_name.description: Name of the task list/column to place the task in (partial match). Example: 'Pending', 'In Progress'. Default: first list in the project.

description.description: Detailed task description. Optional but recommended for complex tasks.

start_on.description: Task start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Default: today or project start date (whichever is later). Must be within the project's date range.

end_on.description: Task due date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional. Must be after start_on and within the project's date range.

assigned_employees.description: Names of employees to assign to this task (partial match). They'll receive a notification. The task creator is always associated but additional assignees are added here.

max_hours.description: Maximum hours budget for this task. Optional.

max_cost.description: Maximum cost budget for this task. Optional.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description:
Update an existing task — change status, progress, dates, assignment, or details.

Resolve the task by name or ID. If ambiguous, also pass project_name to narrow down.
To change task "status", move it to a different task list using task_list_name.
Some lists auto-complete tasks (progress becomes 100) — this happens automatically.

Only pass the fields you want to change. Everything else stays the same.

For assigned_employees: pass the COMPLETE desired list. Existing assignments not in the list
are removed, new ones are added. This replaces, it does not append.

Examples:
- "mark the landing page task as done" → task_name="landing page", task_list_name="Done" or progress=100
- "assign the budget review to Maria" → task_name="budget review", assigned_employees=["Maria"]
- "update progress on the design task to 75%" → task_name="design", progress=75
- "move the API task to In Progress" → task_name="API", task_list_name="In Progress"

task_id.description: Task ID from a previous tool call.

project_name.description: Project name to narrow down task search if ambiguous.

task_list_name.description: Name of the task list/column to move the task to (partial match). Example: 'Done', 'In Progress'.

description.description: New task description.

start_on.description: New start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be within the project's date range.

end_on.description: New due date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be after start_on and within the project's date range.

assigned_employees.description: COMPLETE list of employee names to assign (replaces current assignments). Pass empty array to remove all.

max_hours.description: Maximum hours budget for this task.

max_cost.description: Maximum cost budget for this task.

tools.name: list_personal_todos
tools.description:
List the current user's private personal todos; these are not project tasks.
For project tasks use `create_task`, `list_employee_tasks`, or `update_task`.
For a checklist inside a project task use `get_task_todos`.
The list belongs only to the caller and is never shared with managers or administrators.
Never reopen a completed item just to delete it; reopen only when asked to mark it pending.

status.description: Which personal todos to list. Defaults to pending.

query.description: Search personal todo names by partial match. The first 100 characters are used.

due_on.description: Only todos due exactly on this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

due_before.description: Only todos due on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive.

due_after.description: Only todos due on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive.

response_format.description: Use concise for a checklist or detailed for dates, overdue state, and follow-up IDs.

tools.name: create_personal_todo
tools.description:
Create a private personal todo for the current user; this is not a project task.
For a task on a project or goal use `create_task`; use `list_employee_tasks` and `update_task` for existing project tasks.
For a checklist inside a project task use `get_task_todos`.
Never reopen a completed item just to delete it; reopen only when asked to mark it pending.

name.description: Required name of the private personal todo.

tools.name: update_personal_todo
tools.description:
Update the current user's private personal todo; this is not a project task.
For project tasks use `create_task`, `list_employee_tasks`, or `update_task`.
For a checklist inside a project task use `get_task_todos`.

customer_name.description: Reassign to the customer resolved from this name.

custom_fields.description: CRM custom field values. Use field_uuid, field_id, or exact field_name. Scalar fields use value; datetime values use ISO 8601; select fields use option_ids or option_labels; currency uses value plus optional currency_code.

value.description: Value for boolean, date, time, datetime, string, text, number, or currency fields. Use an empty string or null to clear optional scalar fields.

currency_code.description: Currency code for currency fields, e.g. EUR.

option_ids.description: Option IDs for single_select or multi_select fields. Use an empty array to clear optional selector fields.

option_labels.description: Exact option labels for single_select or multi_select fields.

tools.name: change_opportunity_stage
tools.description:
Move a sales opportunity / deal to a different pipeline stage. The change is recorded in the opportunity's stage history. Find the opportunity by opportunity_id or name and give the target stage by name.
This does not win/lose the deal — for that use close_opportunity.

note.description: Optional note for the stage change.

tools.name: close_opportunity
tools.description:
Close a sales opportunity / deal as WON or LOST. Find it by opportunity_id or name.
A closing factor (reason) is required. For a WON deal the actual amount and its period are also required. The closed date defaults to today. To undo a close, use reopen_opportunity.

closed_on.description: Close date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today. Cannot be in the future.

actual_amount.description: Final amount (required when outcome is won).

actual_amount_period.description: Period of the actual amount (required when won).

tools.name: reopen_opportunity
tools.description: Reopen a closed (won or lost) sales opportunity / deal, returning it to "open". A note explaining why is required. Find it by opportunity_id or name.

tools.name: list_views
tools.description:
List the public pages that can be customized and, for the current account,
whether each one already has an active custom design. Call this first to
discover the view keys, then call list_versions for one of them.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description:
List the versions of a custom view with their name, status (active, published,
draft, unpublished changes) and last-updated time. Read, preview, write and
edit tools take a version by its NAME (matched ignoring case and accents), so
copy the names from here. Pass a view_key from list_views.

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

tools.name: read_view
tools.description:
Read a custom-view version: its master document (verbatim), the tokens
available for that view, and the hard rules for editing it. The returned
master is the ONLY valid base for the "old" snippets you pass to edit_view —
copy from it, never from memory. Read again after any failed edit or at the
start of a new request: the document may have changed in the web editor.

Identify the version by view_key (from list_views) and its name (from
list_versions); names are matched ignoring case and accents.

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

version.description: Name of the version to read (from list_versions), e.g. "Básica".

tools.name: preview_view
tools.description:
Render a version's current master to HTML against sample data, to check the
resulting design without publishing. variant "normal" fills every token;
variant "sparse" leaves optional tokens empty to confirm the design still
holds when data is missing. Returns the rendered body (the CSS is omitted —
it is already in the master you read) plus a preview_url the user can open in
a browser to see the real render with the account's data and full styling.

Identify the version by view_key (from list_views) and its name (from
list_versions); names are matched ignoring case and accents.

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

version.description: Name of the version to preview (from list_versions), e.g. "Básica".

variant.description: Sample data set: "normal" (all tokens) or "sparse" (optional tokens empty). Default: normal.

tools.name: edit_view
tools.description:
Apply changes to a custom-view version's master as an ordered list of literal
{old, new} text replacements. This is where edits to the page are made: each
"old" must appear EXACTLY ONCE in the current master (add surrounding context
to disambiguate) and be copied VERBATIM from the latest read_view or the
master returned by the previous edit — never typed from memory. Use the
shortest unique snippet, not whole blocks: a long "old" fails if a single
character differs.

Use this for targeted changes to the existing design. To rebuild the page
from scratch (a full redesign, or rewriting most of the document), use
write_view instead — recoding the whole document as {old, new} anchors here
would be slow and brittle.

Identify the version by view_key (from list_views) and its name (from
list_versions); names are matched ignoring case and accents.

The edit is atomic and validated server-side: if ANY replacement fails, NONE
are applied and the master is unchanged. On success the full updated master
is returned — base your next edit on it.

On failure the response is an error whose text starts with one of two leads:
- "fixable, try again" (old not found or ambiguous, unknown token, invalid
  CSS): adjust and retry. When an "old" is not found, the error includes the
  closest real region of the document — copy it verbatim. Never resend the
  same batch unchanged.
- "policy limit, do not retry" (scripts, external URLs, iframes, url() in
  CSS): explain the limitation to the user and offer an alternative.

Warnings (non-blocking): missing_apply_button, missing_h1, multiple_h1,
heading_level_skip.

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

version.description: Name of the version to edit (from list_versions), e.g. "Básica".

replacements.description: Ordered list of {old, new}; each old must appear exactly once in the master.

old.description: Exact text to replace (must appear exactly once, copied verbatim).

tools.name: write_view
tools.description: Replace a custom-view version's ENTIRE master with a new document. Use this for a full redesign or when you are rewriting most of the page — NOT for small or targeted changes (for those use edit_view, which is faster and safer for surgical tweaks). Pass the complete new master: HTML + one

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

version.description: Name of the version to rewrite (from list_versions), e.g. "Básica".

master.description: The complete new master document (HTML + one <style> block + token carriers).

tools.name: create_version
tools.description:
Create a new version of a custom view to work on without touching the active
one. By default it starts from the page's default template (the same starting
point the web editor calls "Basic template"); pass "from" (the name of an
existing version) to start from a copy of that version instead.

The new version is a private draft: it is not active and not published, so it
never affects the public page. Publishing and activating stay in the web
editor. After creating, use read_view / write_view / edit_view / preview_view
with the new version's name.

subject.description: Identifier of the record the view belongs to, as shown by list_views (e.g. a booking calendar's slug). Required for per-record views; ignored for account-level views.

name.description: Name for the new version (must be unique for this view), e.g. "Rediseño verano".

from.description: Optional: name of an existing version to copy the design from. Omit to start from the seed.
